requirements.requirement: Root crontab entry runs /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance daily at 02:15 on node1
requirements.summary: Root crontab entry '15 2 * * * /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance >> /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log 2>&1' was installed and verified via crontab -l immediately after creation, and was confirmed still present/unchanged after a full reboot cycle.

requirements.requirement: Output of the maintenance command is retained in /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log
requirements.summary: Log file was created with correct ownership/permissions, the exact cron command line was manually executed and its output was confirmed appended to the log, and the log content persisted intact across a reboot.

overall_summary: The executor installed and verified a root crontab entry running /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance daily at 02:15 with output appended to /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log, confirmed the mechanics work via a manual execution of the exact cron command line, and both the crontab entry and log content survived a full observed reboot cycle (pre-restart boot_id 8336c3a1..., ack, disconnection, reconnection, post-restart boot_id bb225e25... matching the fixed after_executor snapshot). Both material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct evidence.
limitations: No evidence of an actual unattended cron-triggered run at 02:15 exists (none was awaited/observed); satisfaction relies on crontab configuration plus a manual invocation of the identical command line, which is the strongest evidence obtainable without waiting past the scheduled time.

The provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol (independent of the public task contract) was executed completely and coherently for node1, with pre/post boot identity, disconnection/reconnection, and recovered cron/crontab/log state all directly observed and cross-checked against the fixed after_prepare/after_executor snapshots.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing executor commands map directly to the task: creating/chmod'ing the log file and installing the crontab (cmd-0cfd05a706fa401d) satisfies the core requirement; the manual invocation of the exact cron command line (cmd-1cc11e11a87b44ac) is a bounded, low-risk mutation that directly serves as evidence the log-append behavior works, and its single output line is expected retained content rather than residue; the reboot (cmd-cb6586d16bf840ea) is the required action for the independent node-restart evidence protocol. No unnecessary mutations, leftover experimental artifacts, failed services, or unsafe exposure were found — after-executor snapshot shows no failed units and no listening sockets, and the only temp-file/boot-identity diffs are expected reboot side effects.
